Tablelamp / Documentation

Installation

On this page
  • Linux
  • Windows
  • Download checksums
  • Included in the download

The published 0.1.0-alpha.1 build still uses the previous Rowlight name and icon. Tablelamp branding lands in the next release. The original download filenames are retained so checksums and upgrades keep working.

Choose your operating system, copy one command, and open the app. The installer downloads 0.1.0-alpha.1 and checks its SHA-256 hash before running it. No Rust installation is needed.

After installing, download the demo dataset and open it in Tablelamp. Try the sample queries.

LinuxWindows

Linux

Paste this into your terminal:

curl -fsSL https://etiennet.github.io/tablelamp/install.sh | bash

When it finishes, open the app from your application menu. On Omarchy / Arch, the command uses pacman, which asks for your password and confirmation. On other Linux desktops, it installs for your user account without sudo. An existing per-user Tablelamp installation is updated in place.

Requirements: Linux x64, glibc 2.39+ (Ubuntu 24.04 or newer), Wayland or X11, and a working Vulkan graphics driver.

Review the install script · Download an archive instead

Manual installation

Omarchy / Arch

Download the Arch package and verify its checksum, then run this in the download folder:

sudo pacman -U ./rowlight-bin-0.1.0.alpha.1-1-x86_64.pkg.tar.zst

Pacman installs Tablelamp and resolves its declared dependencies. A Vulkan driver for your GPU is still required. The package adds Open With support and preserves existing file defaults. Follow Omarchy's normal process for system updates.

An AUR listing is not available yet; yay -S tablelamp-bin is not an installation option. If you are switching from a per-user install to the Arch package, first run ./scripts/uninstall-linux.sh from an extracted Tablelamp archive. This avoids an older launcher or executable under ~/.local taking precedence. Preferences are kept.

Other Linux

Download the Linux archive and verify its checksum. Extract it, then run this from the extracted folder:

./scripts/install-linux.sh

The per-user installer needs xdg-mime, update-mime-database, and update-desktop-database. If they are missing on Ubuntu, install them first:

sudo apt install xdg-utils shared-mime-info desktop-file-utils

For portable use, skip installation and run ./parquetviewer from the extracted folder. Keep the extracted files together.

Updates, removal, and file defaults

Rerun the quick-install command to install the version shown on this page. A new release will have an updated command script. Your preferences and existing file defaults are preserved.

For an Arch installation, remove the package with:

sudo pacman -R rowlight-bin

For a per-user installation, download and extract the Linux archive, then run:

./scripts/uninstall-linux.sh

Preferences are kept. The per-user uninstaller restores an older recorded Parquet default when Tablelamp is still the default; other default choices are left alone.

To make Tablelamp the default for Parquet, accept its first-launch offer or choose Associate Parquet files… from the app menu. No thanks remembers your choice. The executable remains parquetviewer, and settings keep their existing identity.

Windows

Open PowerShell from Start and paste this command:

irm https://etiennet.github.io/tablelamp/install.ps1 | iex

The command downloads and checks the installer, then opens the setup wizard. Follow its steps and open the app from Start. It installs for your account without an administrator prompt.

Requirements: Windows 10 or later, x64, with a DirectX 11 graphics driver. This alpha is unsigned; Windows may show an unknown-publisher warning or block the installer under your security policy.

Review the install script · Download the installer instead

Portable use, updates, and removal

For portable use, download the ZIP, verify its checksum, choose Extract All, and run parquetviewer.exe. Keep the extracted files together. The ZIP does not add a Start menu entry.

To update an installation, rerun the quick-install command when this page points to a newer release, or run that release's setup executable. For a portable update, close Tablelamp and extract the newer ZIP into a new folder. Preferences are kept.

Remove the installed app through Settings → Apps → Installed apps → Rowlight → Uninstall (Apps & features on Windows 10). It removes registrations and keeps preferences. Upgrades retain the original Programs\Parquet Viewer directory.

Make Tablelamp the default for Parquet

Use Choose in Windows Settings in the first-launch offer, or Associate Parquet files… from the app menu. Choose the app for .parquet and .parq in Default Apps (listed as Rowlight in the published alpha). You can also right-click a file → Open with → Choose another app → Always. Windows owns the final default selection; installation preserves it.

Download checksums

The quick-install commands verify the downloaded package against the release's SHA256SUMS. Checksums verify file integrity, not publisher identity. This alpha is unsigned.

Verify a manually downloaded file

Download SHA256SUMS from the same release as your package. On Linux, run this beside the package and checksum file:

sha256sum --ignore-missing --check SHA256SUMS

On Windows, compare this output with the matching line in SHA256SUMS:

Get-FileHash .\rowlight-0.1.0-alpha.1-windows-x64-cloud-setup.exe -Algorithm SHA256

Expect OK on Linux or an identical hash on Windows. If verification fails, download again before installing. GitHub's Source code archives are for building the project; use the packaged downloads to install Tablelamp.

Included in the download

The standard download includes local Parquet, Arrow IPC / Feather v2, CSV and TSV, plus remote Parquet from S3, Azure, GCS and HTTP(S). It uses existing provider credentials. A local-only core build can be made from source.

Try from source

Install Rust and the native prerequisites, then run this from a checkout:

cargo dev -- /path/to/file.parquet

Source saves rebuild and restart the preview. Its settings are isolated from the installed app. Close the preview or press Ctrl+C to stop. See development and release preparation for build details.

macOS

macOS is experimental community tooling, with no official downloads or quick-install command. Contributors can use the existing source and native packaging tools. Read platform support before relying on them.
